title: "Troubleshooting"
number-sections: true
---

# Where to look

| Node | Log | Content |
|---|---|---|
| head | `/var/log/cfn-init.log`, `/var/log/parallelcluster/` | ParallelCluster bootstrap |
| head | `/var/log/install-pwb-config.log` | Workbench configuration, ALB registration |
| login | `/var/log/config-login.log` | Workbench install (`OnNodeConfigured`) |
| login | `/var/log/rc.pwb.log` | restarts triggered via state files |
| login | `/var/log/rstudio/rstudio-server/`, `/var/log/rstudio/launcher/` | Workbench and Launcher |
| compute | `/opt/rstudio/config-compute/<host>-<time>.log` | session component install |
| image build | `pcluster get-image-log-events`, `/opt/r-install.log`, `/opt/python-install.log` | AMI build |

The nodes are in private subnets. Use SSM Session Manager (`aws ssm start-session --target <instance-id>`) or SSH from inside the VPC. `./cluster-stat.sh <clustername>` lists the instance IDs.

# Common problems

**`deploy.sh` fails with "Pulumi output '...' missing".** The stack is older than the scripts, or you are using the wrong stack name. Run `pulumi up` in `pulumi/`, and check that `STACKNAME`/`CLUSTERNAME` match the stack.

**Cluster creation hangs or the head node times out.** Check `/var/log/install-pwb-config.log` on the head node; the longest steps are the Workbench download and the session components image. Login nodes wait for the head node, so their setup only finishes after it.

**Workbench URL returns 502/503.** The login nodes are not (yet) healthy in the ALB target groups. Check that `pwb-alb-tg-ext-<cluster>` has targets (`aws elbv2 describe-target-health`), and `/var/log/pwb-lb.log` on the login nodes for registration errors. Then check `/var/log/config-login.log` on a login node. It waits for the head node to finish writing the Workbench configuration, so Workbench can come up several minutes after the node itself.

**Sessions start but never connect.** The session on the compute node can't call back into Workbench. Check `launcher-sessions-callback-address` in `/etc/rstudio/rserver.conf`. With `SSL=false` it should be `https://<stack>.<domain>`, the internal ALB. It must resolve and be reachable from the compute nodes.

**Compute nodes fail to start with "rsw-session-....sqsh not found".** The head node builds the session components image in `install-pwb-config.sh`; check its log for download or `mksquashfs` errors. On a compute node, `findmnt /usr/lib/rstudio-server` shows whether the image is mounted.

**`rstudio-server list-nodes` shows nodes that no longer exist.** They are removed when the next login node boots. To remove them right away, run `sudo pwb-lb cleanup` on a login node (log: `/var/log/pwb-lb.log`). Note that `list-nodes` shows stored state; `rstudio-server node-status` probes the nodes.

**Workbench says it is unlicensed or the evaluation has expired.** Check `/var/log/config-login.log` on the login node for a license warning. Run `sudo /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/license-manager status`. Is `pwb_license_key` or `pwb_license_file` set in the Pulumi stack (`pulumi config`)? To activate a running node by hand, run `sudo rstudio-server license-manager activate <key>`, or copy the `.lic` file to `/var/lib/rstudio-server/` and run `sudo rstudio-server restart`.

**Users cannot log in.** Check that the user exists (`id posit0001` on a login node) and that `sssd` is running. Users are created by `just create-users` in `pulumi/`, which needs SSH access to the jump host.

**SimpleAD creation fails.** SimpleAD needs two private subnets in different availability zones. Pulumi takes the first private subnet of each AZ, so the VPC must have private subnets in at least two AZs.

**Database migration errors when Workbench starts.** A Workbench downgrade, or two clusters sharing one database, can leave the `pwb` database in an incompatible state. Each cluster should have its own Pulumi stack (and therefore its own databases).
